user_request: Switch second/quick Pin to vendor/default-PIN quick validation; retain Pixie Dust in offline mode. Also address all normal Pin tasks waiting for beacons.
architecture: wps_defaults provides prefix-matched local candidates, bounded to eight, with a single cached small generator and no per-target cache or network access.

A fixed MIT-licensed upstream implementation is vendored unchanged after the license header; source and SHA256 are recorded. License is also included in bin/third_party_licenses so release assets retain it.
wps_quick validates only complete fixed candidates with Reaver -p, which sets max attempts to one in both supported Reaver versions. Native confirmation is required before writing a success artifact.
An unmatched target is skipped before radio/interface preparation. There is no fallback to brute-force, common-guess batches or Pixie Dust.
The 15-second quick validation budget is independent of normal brute-force settings. Preparation/transport/cleanup time is additional. Incomplete responses are not labelled rejected.
Quick disposable per-candidate sessions never read, import, overwrite or checkpoint normal sessions. Normal state remains in RouterManagerData/wps-sessions, with no legacy-result auto-import.
Shared WPS results, progress and credential-file writer are separated from the execution strategies.
beacon_findings: Newest feedback reports normal Pin, with configured 60-second budget. Last observed native status is waiting for beacon; this is not evidence that the first PIN was rejected.
The two newest native session checkpoints were inspected read-only and have initial P1/P2/state values 0/0/0. They do not demonstrate completed attempts.
Radio-session creation intentionally does not tune channels. The prior WPS path delegated tuning to Reaver without checking actual kernel channel state.
Upstream Reaver 1.6.5/1.6.6 uses the legacy SIOCSIWFREQ WEXT call, and argsparser does not abort when that channel switch fails. A wrong/unset channel can therefore coexist with Waiting for beacon.

WPS now reads owned iw interface state, tunes once through iw/nl80211 only if needed, and verifies actual channel and frequency band before Reaver. Ownership guard checks phy and task token on every operation.
Unconfirmed or mismatched tuning fails before Reaver and follows the existing cleanup path. Normal WPS task budgets are unchanged; no polling/timer workaround or driver change was introduced.
The exact device-side RF failure is not proven by the sanitized archive alone. The tuning gap is code/source verified; real-device acceptance remains pending.

verification.ui_render: Quick dialog visually inspected; existing light/dark active-row tests passed.

acceptance: Exit the old process normally and reopen the source app.

Select one authorized known-WPS target. Normal Pin must log successful kernel channel verification before running. If tuning fails, capture the precise error; it must not spend 60 seconds waiting for a beacon.
If the tool reports Trying pin, progress must display that exact candidate and highlight only that target. No reported candidate means no submitted-PIN claim.
Quick Pin skips unknown profiles; confirmed native rejection advances candidates, while connection failures remain incomplete.
restart_state: Old pythonw processes were still present at last check; normal exit requested from user. No forced termination or live router operation was performed.
